newsitem.title: UK: British millers eye Canadian wheat quota.
newsitem.headline: British millers eye Canadian wheat quota.

text.p: British millers will be very interested in the 300,000 tonnes of duty free high quality wheat the EU is due to import, a milling source said.

The European Union has not yet set a date for fixing details of a tender to import the wheat, such as the split between durum and soft wheat and the number and timing of tranches, a European Commission official said on Friday.
British millers expect to be sharing the quota, which is aimed at Canadian suppliers, with other European importers, the milling source said.
"British millers do have a strong interest in the quota," the source said.
"But some of it will be durum wheat and we only want common wheat," the source said.

And there would be strong competition from other European destinations for the wheat. "On previous occasions there has been substantial overbidding, with a resultant scaling down by means of a co-efficient," he said.

The high protein content foreseen in the specification for quality wheat allowed in under this concession creates further uncertainty, the source said. He doubted whether Canada would be in a position to supply the necessary amount of wheat. "The U.S. may benefit," he said.
Although the tender is aimed at Canada, world trade rules mean that any country may supply the wheat. --Christopher Lyddon, London newsroom +44 171 542 7928
